message.content:
This appears to be based on a CBP ruling about framed film cell displays. Candidates are 9706 (antiques over 100 years old), 9705 (collections and collectors' pieces of historical, ethnographic, or cinematographic interest), 4911 (printed pictures), 3924, and 4414 (wooden frames).

Heading 9705 covers "Collections and collectors' pieces of zoological, botanical, mineralogical, anatomical, historical, archaeological, paleontological, ethnographic or numismatic interest." Cinematographic film cells are not clearly within it. Heading 3706 covers cinematographic film, exposed and developed, and 3706.10 covers film of a width of 35 mm or more. The displays contain actual 35mm film cells, but as a framed article the whole is more likely classified as wall decor. Plastic framed wall art would fall under 3924.90 or 3926.40 (statuettes and other ornamental articles of plastics). A framed montage with a poster graphic would more likely be 4911.91 (printed pictures), but the essential character is arguably the film cells.

I recall a CBP ruling for a similar "film cell" display classifying it under 9706 or 3926.40. The film cells are not antiques, so 9706 is out. I'm going with 3926.40.0000, ornamental articles of plastics, since the plastic frame and Perspex dominate. The current 10-digit code is 3926.40.0000, since the 2012 schedule has 3926.40.00 with a 10-digit statistical suffix of 00.

{"hts_code": "3926.40.0000", "reason": "The framed, Perspex-covered decorative wall display of film cells, poster graphic and plaque is an ornamental article whose plastic frame and cover give it its essential character, so it falls under other ornamental articles of plastics."}

predicted_reason: The framed, Perspex-covered decorative wall display of film cells, poster graphic and plaque is an ornamental article whose plastic frame and cover give it its essential character, so it falls under other ornamental articles of plastics.
